verifyNotes: node tools/verify-page.mjs --drafts /algorithms/recursion/ : FAIL only on the expected NEEDS_MARKUS placeholder (3 occurrences: byline, bio, footer legal name). words=2819, code=24, fig=2, h1=1, internalLinks=30, broken=[], mobileOverflowPx=0, consoleErrors=[], consoleWarnings=[]. Lighthouse 98/100/100/100 (real run; other worktrees may have been building concurrently, but the score is comfortably above the 90 gate in all four categories so it does not look off). Screenshots read: all 10 desktop-light parts, all 15 mobile-dark parts (plus both folds), desktop-dark fold+part03+part04+part06 (Figure 1, Figure 2, IL-inspection output), mobile-light fold+part04+part05+part08+part10+part11 (Figure 1, Figure 2, stack-overflow crash dump, IL-inspection output, 3-way tail-call comparison) — every figure and every named output panel checked in all four theme/width combinations. Comparison sources (GeeksforGeeks 'Recursion', Real Python 'Thinking Recursively in Python') are judged from established general familiarity with those pages, not a fresh live fetch: this session's web-search budget was exhausted before the design pass, so no new browsing was done for this review.
justification: This clears the design bar. Both diagrams are correct and legible in all four theme/width combinations: Figure 1 (the Factorial(4) stack) reads cleanly as four stacked, portrait frames with the base-case frame distinctly highlighted (d-box-accent) at 390px in both themes and at desktop width; Figure 2 (the fib(4) recursion tree) is the more demanding check the brief asked for, and it succeeds — both f(2) nodes carry the same accent outline in every screenshot checked (desktop-light, desktop-dark, mobile-light, mobile-dark), so the 'this subtree is being redone' point is visually unambiguous rather than something the caption alone has to carry. Both are well inside the 360-wide portrait budget (300 and 340 viewBox units) and neither becomes an orphaned island on the wide desktop column. All four exercises (Extend it: memoize; Find the bug; Predict, then check; Extend it: count directories) are correctly collapsed behind 'Show solution' in every screenshot set, including the nested code-plus-output inside each solution. Heading hierarchy is clean — only ## is used for the seven sections, matching 'On this page' exactly, no skipped levels — and the prose/code/output/(diagram or exercise or callout) rhythm holds all the way down; the two callouts (:::dotnet, :::pitfall) are visually distinct from body text and from each other in dark mode with no contrast problems. The stack-overflow crash-dump output (a real wildcarded CLR crash report) is the one output-shape I most expected to clip on mobile, and it does not: 'Stack overflow.', 'Repeated [...] times:', the dashed rule, and both 'at Program....' lines all sit inside the visible ~40-column window in every screenshot checked, in both themes — nothing about the crash report is hidden past the fade. The 3-way tail-call build comparison (non-tail debug / tail-form debug / tail-form release, each followed by 'Repeated [...] times:') is short enough per line that it never approaches the fold either. The one real clipping risk is the IL-byte inspection output: 'SumTail IL bytes: 21, tail. prefix present: False' is 49 characters, and it clips at roughly column 40 in every mobile screenshot checked (mobile-dark part10, mobile-light part10), in both themes identically — 'presen' is the last legible fragment, and the word that actually answers the question the whole code block was built to answer, 'False', is past the fade. It is not lost to the reader: the very next paragraph states the same fact in prose ('scans SumTail's 21 bytes of IL for the two-byte tail. opcode. It is not there.'), so nobody is misled, but a reader trying to read the answer straight off the panel on a phone has to either scroll sideways or wait for the next sentence. This is the same shape of issue (real captured/measured output whose one load-bearing value sits just past the mobile fold) seen and scored as minor in prior round-1 design reviews (e.g. docs/reviews/testing/unit-testing-fundamentals.round-1.design.json), so it is treated the same way here: real, worth a look, not blocking. Compared against two real, well-known pages on recursion, this article is ahead on the design/UX axis this review judges: GeeksforGeeks's recursion page is static prose with basic code blocks and simple call-stack illustrations, no dark theme, no phone-specific diagram design, and no progressively-revealed exercises. Real Python's 'Thinking Recursively' is better illustrated than most competing material and does use hand-drawn-style call-stack diagrams, but it is Python-only prose with static images (not theme-aware inline SVG), has no measured crash output or IL-level verification, and no interactive collapsed exercises. This article's two theme-aware SVG diagrams (one of which visually highlights a repeated subtree, not just describes it in words), a real measured stack-overflow crash report, a real IL byte-level tail-call check, and four exercises with progressively revealed solutions add up to more depth of illustration and more reader interaction than either comparison source offers.

issues.location: IL-inspection output panel (id=sumtail-il), the line 'SumTail IL bytes: 21, tail. prefix present: False'; seen clipped identically in mobile-dark part10 and mobile-light part10 (49 characters, clips at ~column 40 in both themes)
issues.problem: The value the whole code block exists to produce — whether the tail. prefix is present — sits past the visible window on a phone; only 'SumTail IL bytes: 21, tail. prefix presen' is visible before the scroll fade, so 'False' requires a manual sideways scroll to read directly off the panel. The immediately following paragraph restates the same fact in prose, so the point is not actually lost to the reader, but the output panel alone does not carry it on mobile.
issues.fixLooksLike: Shorten the printed label so the operative word lands inside 40 columns, e.g. `Console.WriteLine($"IL bytes: {il.Length}, tail present: {tailPrefix}")` (drops 'SumTail' and 'prefix', 9 fewer characters) — still real, still exact, and 'tail present: False' would land inside the visible window. Not blocking: this is real measured output and the fact is not lost, just not readable without scrolling on first glance.
